notes: Same overall gap as iteration 1 (100% vs ~74%), now over 6 cases and 27 checks, including 2 cases backed by real git repos.

tidy-up-review is the strongest new signal (6/6 vs 3/6): without the skill the agent kept the stale promoted rule ('overlap is intended'), treated the journal as add-only, and proposed no promotion. Demotion, cost-based promotion and journal expiry only happen with the skill.

commit-guard-emptied-file does not discriminate: the baseline also noticed the emptied file from git status/diff. The guard's value is as a backstop for bulk commits inside longer routines, which this case doesn't exercise.

Skill friction found: (1) commit.md doesn't say what to do when git has no identity (both git-case runs improvised by reusing the repo's author); (2) review's journal expiry deletes a file, which check-commit then flags, so the user is effectively asked twice.

Baseline secret-capture wrote a pointer note claiming the credentials are in the password manager under 'staging db', which the user never said. The skill run offered the pointer instead of inventing it.
Cost: about 7.8k more tokens and 13s more per run with the skill. The review case is the most expensive (63k tokens, 79s), because it runs several script checks.
